name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q01 - Classification of monohydric dihydric allylic vinylic benzylic alcohols

questiontext.text:
Match the compounds in List-I with their correct classification in List-II.

List-I (Compound)List-II (Classification)
(a) \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2OH}\)(i) Dihydric alcohol
(b) \(\mathrm{HO-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\)(ii) Allylic alcohol
(c) \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-OH}\)(iii) Benzylic alcohol
(d) \(\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2OH}\)(iv) Vinylic alcohol

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Alcohols are classified based on the number of hydroxyl (\(-\mathrm{OH}\)) groups and the hybridisation and position of the carbon atom to which the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group is attached.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Compound
1. In \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2OH}\), the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group is attached to an \(sp^3\) hybridised carbon atom adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond, so it is an allylic alcohol.
2. In \(\mathrm{HO-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\) (ethane-1,2-diol), there are two hydroxyl groups present in the molecule, so it is a dihydric alcohol.
3. In \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-OH}\), the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group is bonded directly to an \(sp^2\) hybridised carbon of a carbon-carbon double bond, so it is a vinylic alcohol.
4. In \(\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2OH}\), the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group is attached to an \(sp^3\) hybridised carbon atom directly next to an aromatic ring, so it is a benzylic alcohol.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2OH}\) is an allylic alcohol, \(\mathrm{HO-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\) is a dihydric alcohol, \(\mathrm{CH_2=CH-OH}\) is a vinylic alcohol, and \(\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2OH}\) is a benzylic alcohol, which corresponds to (a)-(ii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q02 - Common and IUPAC names of polyhydric phenols and glycerol

questiontext.text:
Match the common names in List-I with their corresponding IUPAC names in List-II.

List-I (Common Name)List-II (IUPAC Name)
(a) Catechol(i) Benzene-1,3-diol
(b) Resorcinol(ii) Propane-1,2,3-triol
(c) Hydroquinone(iii) Benzene-1,2-diol
(d) Glycerol(iv) Benzene-1,4-diol

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Polyhydric phenols are named as benzenediols using locants for the positions of the two \(-\mathrm{OH}\) groups, while polyhydric aliphatic alcohols retain the final 'e' of the alkane followed by the multiplicative prefix and 'ol'.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Compound
1. Catechol is the 1,2-dihydroxy derivative of benzene, so its IUPAC name is benzene-1,2-diol.
2. Resorcinol is the 1,3-dihydroxy derivative of benzene, so its IUPAC name is benzene-1,3-diol.
3. Hydroquinone (or quinol) is the 1,4-dihydroxy derivative of benzene, so its IUPAC name is benzene-1,4-diol.
4. Glycerol has three \(-\mathrm{OH}\) groups on a three-carbon propane chain (\(\mathrm{HOCH_2-CH(OH)-CH_2OH}\)), so its IUPAC name is propane-1,2,3-triol.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Matching each common name to its IUPAC name gives (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q03 - Common and IUPAC names of aromatic ethers and cresols

questiontext.text:
Match the common names in List-I with their IUPAC names in List-II.

List-I (Common Name)List-II (IUPAC Name)
(a) Anisole(i) 4-Methylphenol
(b) Phenetole(ii) Ethoxybenzene
(c) o-Cresol(iii) Methoxybenzene
(d) p-Cresol(iv) 2-Methylphenol

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In IUPAC nomenclature, aryl alkyl ethers are named as alkoxyarenes (taking the benzene ring as the parent hydrocarbon), and methyl-substituted phenols are numbered starting from the carbon bearing the \(-\mathrm{OH}\) group.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Compound
1. Anisole is methyl phenyl ether (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5OCH_3}\)), whose IUPAC name is methoxybenzene.
2. Phenetole is ethyl phenyl ether (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5OC_2H_5}\)), whose IUPAC name is ethoxybenzene.
3. o-Cresol has a methyl group at the 1,2-position relative to \(-\mathrm{OH}\), so its IUPAC name is 2-methylphenol.
4. p-Cresol has a methyl group at the 1,4-position relative to \(-\mathrm{OH}\), so its IUPAC name is 4-methylphenol.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iii), (b)-(ii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q04 - Structural bond lengths and bond angles of functional groups

questiontext.text:
Match the structural parameters in List-I with their experimental values in List-II.

List-I (Structural Parameter)List-II (Value)
(a) \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}\) bond length in methanol(i) \(136\text{ pm}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}\) bond length in phenol(ii) \(111.7^\circ\)
(c) \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) bond angle in methanol(iii) \(142\text{ pm}\)
(d) \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{C}\) bond angle in methoxymethane(iv) \(108.9^\circ\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In alcohols, phenols, and ethers, oxygen is \(sp^3\) hybridised. Bond lengths are affected by carbon hybridisation and resonance delocalisation, while bond angles are governed by lone-pair repulsion versus steric repulsion between alkyl groups.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Parameter
1. In methanol, oxygen is bonded to an \(sp^3\) carbon by a single \(\sigma\) bond, giving a \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}\) bond length of \(142\text{ pm}\).
2. In phenol, conjugation of the oxygen lone pair with the aromatic ring imparts partial double bond character and the carbon is \(sp^2\) hybridised, shortening the \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}\) bond length to \(136\text{ pm}\).
3. In methanol, lone pair-lone pair repulsion on oxygen compresses the \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{H}\) bond angle slightly below the tetrahedral angle (\(109.5^\circ\)) to \(108.9^\circ\).
4. In methoxymethane, steric repulsion between the two bulky methyl groups widens the \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{C}\) bond angle slightly beyond the tetrahedral angle to \(111.7^\circ\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q05 - Preparation of alcohols from alkenes carbonyls and Grignard reagents

questiontext.text:
Match the reactions in List-I with their major alcohol products in List-II.

List-I (Reaction)List-II (Major Product)
(a) \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH_2 + H_2O \xrightarrow{H^+}}\)(i) \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH_2 \xrightarrow{(i)\ B_2H_6,\ (ii)\ H_2O_2/OH^-}}\)(ii) \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\)
(c) \(\mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH_3 \xrightarrow{(i)\ CH_3MgBr,\ (ii)\ H_2O}}\)(iii) \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3}\)
(d) \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CHO \xrightarrow{H_2/Pd}}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-OH}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Alcohols are prepared from alkenes by acid-catalysed hydration (Markovnikov addition) or hydroboration-oxidation (anti-Markovnikov addition), from ketones/aldehydes by Grignard addition, and from aldehydes by catalytic hydrogenation.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Analysis of Each Reaction
1. Acid-catalysed hydration of propene follows Markovnikov's rule via the more stable secondary carbocation, giving propan-2-ol (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3}\)).
2. Hydroboration-oxidation of propene proceeds with boron adding to the less substituted carbon, giving the net anti-Markovnikov product propan-1-ol (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\)).
3. Reaction of propanone (a ketone) with methylmagnesium bromide followed by hydrolysis yields a tertiary alcohol, 2-methylpropan-2-ol (\(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-OH}\)).
4. Catalytic reduction of butanal with \(\mathrm{H_2/Pd}\) reduces the aldehyde group to a primary alcohol, butan-1-ol (\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q06 - Starting materials and reagents for preparation of phenols

questiontext.text:
Match the starting materials in List-I with the reagents/conditions required to convert them into phenol in List-II.

List-I (Starting Material)List-II (Reagents / Conditions)
(a) Chlorobenzene(i) \(\mathrm{H_2O}\), warm
(b) Benzenesulphonic acid(ii) \(\mathrm{O_2}\) followed by \(\mathrm{H^+/H_2O}\)
(c) Benzene diazonium chloride(iii) \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) at \(623\text{ K},\ 300\text{ atm}\), then \(\mathrm{HCl}\)
(d) Cumene(iv) Molten \(\mathrm{NaOH}\), then \(\mathrm{H^+}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phenols can be synthesised from haloarenes, arylsulphonic acids, diazonium salts, and cumene using characteristic reagents and temperature/pressure conditions.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Method
1. Chlorobenzene requires drastic conditions (\(\mathrm{NaOH}\) at \(623\text{ K}\) and \(300\text{ atm}\)) to form sodium phenoxide, which is acidified with \(\mathrm{HCl}\) to give phenol.
2. Benzenesulphonic acid is heated with molten \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) to form sodium phenoxide, followed by acidification (\(\mathrm{H^+}\)) to yield phenol.
3. Benzene diazonium chloride is readily hydrolysed to phenol simply by warming with water (\(\mathrm{H_2O}\)).
4. Cumene (isopropylbenzene) is oxidised with \(\mathrm{O_2}\) to cumene hydroperoxide, which on treatment with dilute acid (\(\mathrm{H^+/H_2O}\)) gives phenol and acetone.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q07 - Acid strength and pKa values of phenols and ethanol

questiontext.text:
Match the compounds in List-I with their approximate \(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}\) values in List-II.

List-I (Compound)List-II (\(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}\))
(a) p-Nitrophenol(i) \(10.0\)
(b) m-Nitrophenol(ii) \(15.9\)
(c) Phenol(iii) \(7.1\)
(d) Ethanol(iv) \(8.3\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A lower \(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}\) value corresponds to a stronger acid. Electron-withdrawing groups such as \(-\mathrm{NO_2}\) stabilise the phenoxide ion and increase acid strength, especially at the ortho and para positions due to resonance.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Comparison
1. p-Nitrophenol has a strong \(-R\) and \(-I\) nitro group at the para position, strongly stabilising the conjugate base, giving the lowest \(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}\) of \(7.1\).
2. m-Nitrophenol has the nitro group at the meta position (acting only via \(-I\) effect), so it is less acidic than p-nitrophenol but more acidic than phenol, with \(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a} = 8.3\).
3. Unsubstituted phenol has a resonance-stabilised phenoxide ion and a \(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a}\) of \(10.0\).
4. Ethanol forms an unstabilised ethoxide ion with localised negative charge on oxygen, making it much less acidic than phenol, with \(\mathrm{p}K_\mathrm{a} = 15.9\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q08 - Reagents for oxidation bromination and dehydration reactions

questiontext.text:
Match the chemical conversions in List-I with the appropriate reagents in List-II.

List-I (Conversion)List-II (Reagent)
(a) Primary alcohol to carboxylic acid(i) \(\mathrm{PCC}\)
(b) Primary alcohol to aldehyde(ii) \(85\%\ \mathrm{H_3PO_4}\) at \(440\text{ K}\)
(c) Phenol to 2,4,6-tribromophenol(iii) Acidified \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\)
(d) Propan-2-ol to propene(iv) Bromine water (\(\mathrm{Br_2/H_2O}\))

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Specific reagents control the extent of oxidation, degree of electrophilic bromination, and dehydration of alcohols.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Conversion
1. Acidified \(\mathrm{KMnO_4}\) is a strong oxidising agent that oxidises primary alcohols directly to carboxylic acids.
2. Pyridinium chlorochromate (\(\mathrm{PCC}\)) is a mild oxidising agent that stops oxidation of primary alcohols at the aldehyde stage.
3. Treating phenol with bromine water (\(\mathrm{Br_2/H_2O}\)) produces a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol.
4. Propan-2-ol (a secondary alcohol) undergoes dehydration to propene on heating with \(85\%\ \mathrm{H_3PO_4}\) at \(440\text{ K}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q09 - Named reactions of phenols and their major products

questiontext.text:
Match the reactions of phenols in List-I with their major products in List-II.

List-I (Reaction)List-II (Major Product)
(a) Kolbe's reaction(i) Salicylaldehyde
(b) Reimer-Tiemann reaction(ii) Benzoquinone
(c) Acetylation of salicylic acid(iii) Salicylic acid
(d) Oxidation of phenol with \(\mathrm{Na_2Cr_2O_7/H_2SO_4}\)(iv) Aspirin

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Phenols undergo characteristic electrophilic substitution, esterification, and oxidation reactions yielding distinct aromatic products.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Reaction
1. In Kolbe's reaction, sodium phenoxide reacts with \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) followed by acidification to yield 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid).
2. In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, phenol reacts with \(\mathrm{CHCl_3}\) and aqueous \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) followed by acidification to introduce a \(-\mathrm{CHO}\) group at the ortho position, giving salicylaldehyde.
3. Acetylation of salicylic acid with acetic anhydride in the presence of \(\mathrm{H^+}\) produces acetylsalicylic acid, commonly known as aspirin.
4. Oxidation of phenol with chromic acid (\(\mathrm{Na_2Cr_2O_7/H_2SO_4}\)) yields a conjugated diketone, benzoquinone.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q10 - Reactions of alcohols with heated copper and sulphuric acid

questiontext.text:
Match the reactions in List-I with their major products in List-II.

List-I (Reaction)List-II (Major Product)
(a) \(\mathrm{RCH_2OH \xrightarrow{Cu,\ 573\ K}}\)(i) Ketone
(b) \(\mathrm{R-CH(OH)-R' \xrightarrow{Cu,\ 573\ K}}\)(ii) 2-Methylpropene
(c) \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-OH \xrightarrow{Cu,\ 573\ K}}\)(iii) Ethoxyethane
(d) \(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{H_2SO_4,\ 413\ K}}\)(iv) Aldehyde

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
When vapours of alcohols are passed over heated copper at \(573\text{ K}\), primary and secondary alcohols undergo dehydrogenation, whereas tertiary alcohols undergo dehydration. With \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\), ethanol forms an ether at \(413\text{ K}\) (and ethene at \(443\text{ K}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Reaction
1. Primary alcohol (\(\mathrm{RCH_2OH}\)) over \(\mathrm{Cu}\) at \(573\text{ K}\) loses \(\mathrm{H_2}\) to give an aldehyde (\(\mathrm{RCHO}\)).
2. Secondary alcohol (\(\mathrm{R-CH(OH)-R'}\)) over \(\mathrm{Cu}\) at \(573\text{ K}\) loses \(\mathrm{H_2}\) to give a ketone (\(\mathrm{R-CO-R'}\)).
3. Tertiary alcohol (\(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-OH}\)) has no \(\alpha\)-hydrogen and undergoes dehydration over \(\mathrm{Cu}\) at \(573\text{ K}\) to give 2-methylpropene.
4. Ethanol heated with \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) at \(413\text{ K}\) undergoes bimolecular dehydration (\(\mathrm{S_N2}\)) to give ethoxyethane.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q11 - Boiling points of propane methoxymethane ethanol and butanol

questiontext.text:
Match the compounds in List-I with their boiling points in List-II.

List-I (Compound)List-II (Boiling Point)
(a) Propane(i) \(351\text{ K}\)
(b) Methoxymethane(ii) \(390\text{ K}\)
(c) Ethanol(iii) \(231\text{ K}\)
(d) Butan-1-ol(iv) \(248\text{ K}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Boiling points depend on intermolecular forces (hydrogen bonding > dipole-dipole interactions > van der Waals dispersion forces) and molecular mass (larger carbon chain increases van der Waals forces).

Step 2: Step-by-Step Comparison
1. Propane (molecular mass \(44\)) is a non-polar alkane with only weak dispersion forces, so it has the lowest boiling point (\(231\text{ K}\)).
2. Methoxymethane (molecular mass \(46\)) is a weakly polar ether lacking intermolecular hydrogen bonding, so its boiling point is \(248\text{ K}\).
3. Ethanol (molecular mass \(46\)) exhibits strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding, raising its boiling point to \(351\text{ K}\).
4. Butan-1-ol has both intermolecular hydrogen bonding and a longer four-carbon chain (higher molecular mass and stronger van der Waals forces than ethanol), giving it the highest boiling point (\(390\text{ K}\)).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q12 - Cleavage of unsymmetrical alkyl and aryl ethers with HI

questiontext.text:
Match the ethers in List-I with the major products formed when each is heated with \(\mathrm{HI}\) (1 equivalent) in List-II.

List-I (Ether)List-II (Major Products)
(a) \(\mathrm{CH_3-O-CH_2CH_3}\)(i) \(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH + CH_3I}\)
(b) \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-O-CH_3}\)(ii) \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-I + CH_3OH}\)
(c) \(\mathrm{C_6H_5-O-CH_3}\)(iii) \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2I + C_6H_5OH}\)
(d) \(\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2-O-C_6H_5}\)(iv) \(\mathrm{CH_3I + CH_3CH_2OH}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Protonation of an ether by \(\mathrm{HI}\) is followed by \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}\) cleavage. For primary/secondary alkyl ethers, \(\mathrm{I^-}\) attacks the less sterically hindered carbon via \(\mathrm{S_N2}\). When a tertiary alkyl group is present, cleavage proceeds via \(\mathrm{S_N1}\) to form a stable tertiary carbocation. In alkyl aryl ethers, the strong \(\mathrm{C_{aryl}}-\mathrm{O}\) bond is never cleaved.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Analysis of Each Ether
1. In \(\mathrm{CH_3-O-CH_2CH_3}\), both alkyl groups are primary, so \(\mathrm{I^-}\) attacks the less hindered methyl carbon by \(\mathrm{S_N2}\), yielding \(\mathrm{CH_3I + CH_3CH_2OH}\).
2. In \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-O-CH_3}\), departure of \(\mathrm{CH_3OH}\) from the protonated ether forms the stable tertiary carbocation \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C^+}\), which combines with \(\mathrm{I^-}\) to give \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-I + CH_3OH}\).
3. In anisole (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5-O-CH_3}\)), the \(\mathrm{O-C_6H_5}\) bond is stronger due to \(sp^2\) carbon and partial double bond character, so cleavage occurs at the \(\mathrm{O-CH_3}\) bond to give \(\mathrm{C_6H_5OH + CH_3I}\).
4. In benzyl phenyl ether (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2-O-C_6H_5}\)), the \(\mathrm{O-C_6H_5}\) bond remains intact while the \(\mathrm{CH_2-O}\) bond cleaves to yield \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2I + C_6H_5OH}\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iv), (b)-(ii), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q13 - Williamson ether synthesis reactants and elimination competition

questiontext.text:
Match the Williamson synthesis reactions in List-I with their major organic products in List-II.

List-I (Reactants)List-II (Major Product)
(a) \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-ONa + CH_3Br}\)(i) 2-Methylpropene
(b) \(\mathrm{CH_3ONa + (CH_3)_3C-Br}\)(ii) 1-Methoxy-4-nitrobenzene
(c) \(\mathrm{C_6H_5ONa + C_2H_5Br}\)(iii) tert-Butyl methyl ether
(d) \(\mathrm{4\text{-}O_2N\text{-}C_6H_4\text{-}ONa + CH_3Br}\)(iv) Ethoxybenzene

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Williamson synthesis proceeds by \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) attack of an alkoxide or phenoxide ion on a primary alkyl halide. When a tertiary alkyl halide is used, the strongly basic alkoxide promotes elimination over substitution.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Analysis of Each Reaction
1. \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-ONa + CH_3Br}\) uses a primary alkyl halide (\(\mathrm{CH_3Br}\)), so \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) substitution succeeds cleanly to give tert-butyl methyl ether.
2. \(\mathrm{CH_3ONa + (CH_3)_3C-Br}\) involves a tertiary alkyl halide; sodium methoxide acts as a strong base and causes elimination to give 2-methylpropene exclusively.
3. Sodium phenoxide (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5ONa}\)) reacts with bromoethane (\(\mathrm{C_2H_5Br}\)) via \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) to give ethoxybenzene.
4. Sodium 4-nitrophenoxide reacts with \(\mathrm{CH_3Br}\) via \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) to yield 1-methoxy-4-nitrobenzene.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q14 - Electrophilic aromatic substitution of phenol and anisole

questiontext.text:
Match the electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions in List-I with their major products in List-II.

List-I (Reaction)List-II (Major Product)
(a) Phenol + \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) in \(\mathrm{CS_2}\) at \(273\text{ K}\)(i) 4-Bromoanisole
(b) Anisole + \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) in ethanoic acid(ii) 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol
(c) Anisole + \(\mathrm{CH_3COCl / anhyd.\ AlCl_3}\)(iii) 4-Bromophenol
(d) Phenol + \(\mathrm{Conc.\ HNO_3}\)(iv) 4-Methoxyacetophenone

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Both \(-\mathrm{OH}\) and \(-\mathrm{OR}\) groups strongly activate the benzene ring and are ortho, para-directing. Due to steric factors, the para-substituted isomer is generally the major product in monofunctionalisation.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Analysis of Each Reaction
1. Phenol with \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) in a low-polarity solvent (\(\mathrm{CS_2}\)) at \(273\text{ K}\) undergoes monobromination, giving 4-bromophenol as the major product.
2. Anisole with \(\mathrm{Br_2}\) in ethanoic acid gives p-bromoanisole (4-bromoanisole) in \(90\%\) yield.
3. Friedel-Crafts acetylation of anisole with ethanoyl chloride (\(\mathrm{CH_3COCl}\)) in the presence of anhydrous \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\) gives 4-methoxyacetophenone as the major product.
4. Phenol treated with concentrated \(\mathrm{HNO_3}\) undergoes trisubstitution to yield 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q15 - Commercial alcohol synthesis enzymes and Lucas reagent

questiontext.text:
Match the enzymes, catalysts, or reagents in List-I with their specific roles in List-II.

List-I (Enzyme / Catalyst / Reagent)List-II (Role / Reaction)
(a) Invertase(i) Conversion of glucose/fructose to ethanol and \(\mathrm{CO_2}\)
(b) Zymase(ii) Immediate turbidity with tertiary alcohols
(c) \(\mathrm{ZnO-Cr_2O_3}\) at \(573\text{--}673\text{ K},\ 200\text{--}300\text{ atm}\)(iii) Hydrolysis of sucrose to glucose and fructose
(d) Lucas reagent (conc. \(\mathrm{HCl + ZnCl_2}\))(iv) Industrial synthesis of methanol from \(\mathrm{CO + 2H_2}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Commercial production of ethanol by fermentation uses yeast enzymes, commercial methanol synthesis uses catalytic hydrogenation of carbon monoxide, and Lucas reagent distinguishes primary, secondary, and tertiary alcohols.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Item
1. Invertase catalyses the hydrolysis of sucrose (\(\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}\)) into glucose and fructose.
2. Zymase (found in yeast) converts glucose and fructose into ethanol and \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) under anaerobic conditions.
3. \(\mathrm{ZnO-Cr_2O_3}\) at \(573\text{--}673\text{ K}\) and \(200\text{--}300\text{ atm}\) catalyses the hydrogenation of \(\mathrm{CO}\) with \(2\mathrm{H_2}\) to produce methanol.
4. Lucas reagent (concentrated \(\mathrm{HCl}\) and anhydrous \(\mathrm{ZnCl_2}\)) reacts with tertiary alcohols to produce immediate turbidity due to rapid formation of insoluble alkyl halides.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ALCOHOLSPHENOLSETHERS_MCQ_Q16 - Dehydration and carbocation rearrangement products of alcohols

questiontext.text:
Match the alcohol reactions in List-I with their major products in List-II.

List-I (Reaction)List-II (Major Product)
(a) 1-Methylcyclohexanol + \(\mathrm{H^+/Heat}\)(i) But-2-ene
(b) Butan-1-ol + \(\mathrm{H^+/Heat}\)(ii) 2-Methylpropene
(c) 2-Methylpropan-2-ol + \(20\%\ \mathrm{H_3PO_4}\) at \(358\text{ K}\)(iii) 1-Methylcyclohexene
(d) 3-Methylbutan-2-ol + \(\mathrm{HBr}\)(iv) 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Acid-catalysed dehydration and reaction of alcohols with \(\mathrm{HBr}\) involve carbocation intermediates that can rearrange to more stable carbocations, and dehydration favours the more substituted alkene.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Analysis of Each Reaction
1. 1-Methylcyclohexanol forms a tertiary carbocation and loses a proton to yield the more substituted endo-cyclic alkene, 1-methylcyclohexene.
2. Butan-1-ol undergoes dehydration via rearrangement of the primary carbocation to a secondary carbocation, yielding but-2-ene as the major product.
3. 2-Methylpropan-2-ol (a tertiary alcohol) dehydrates under mild conditions (\(20\%\ \mathrm{H_3PO_4}\) at \(358\text{ K}\)) to form 2-methylpropene.
4. 3-Methylbutan-2-ol with \(\mathrm{HBr}\) forms a secondary carbocation that rearranges via a \(1,2\)-hydride shift to a more stable tertiary carbocation, giving 2-bromo-2-methylbutane.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv).
